chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥajjāl and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from a man from the people of al-Madīnah, from al-Muṭarrifī, who said:

Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام passed away, and he owed me four thousand dirhams. So I said to myself, “My wealth is gone.” Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام sent word to me: “When tomorrow comes, come to me, and let there be with you a scale and weights.” So I entered upon Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and he said to me: “Abū al-Ḥasan has passed away, and he owes you four thousand dirhams.” I said, “Yes.” Then he lifted the prayer mat that was beneath him, and there were dinars beneath it, so he handed them over to me.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: four thousand dirhams owed as a debt

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام knowing and repaying a debt owed by Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that after Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام passed away, a man feared the loss of money owed to him. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام informed him of the exact debt and repaid it, manifesting knowledge and the fulfillment of the rights of others.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal and Amro Bin usman, from a man from the peple of Al medina, from Al Mutarrafy who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> passed away and for me, upon him<sup>asws</sup>, were four thousand Dirham. So I said within myself, ‘My wealth has gone!’. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> (9<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) sent a message to me: ‘When it is the morning, come to me<sup>asws</sup>, and let there happen to be a scale with you and weights’. So I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> has passed away, and for you, upon him<sup>asws</sup>, are four thousand Dirhams’. So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> raised the prayer mat which was beneath him, and there were Dirans under it, so he<sup>asws</sup> handed these over to me’.
